# Wave 3 transcript parser: Python 3.10 independent review

## Verdict: PASS for the reviewed patch

The pending parser patch closes the Python 3.10 legacy-renderer skip bypass. I independently exercised the exact parser bytes with **actual CPython 3.10.22** and **CPython 3.12.14**. Each runtime rejected all 64 negative probes, including all six previously failing lifecycle/cleanup variants and 30 additional quoted, empty, and multiline skip-reason variants. There were zero incorrect acceptances. Each runtime also accepted all 651 original test records.

### Exact source binding

| Reviewed object | Identity |
|---|---|
| Base commit | `44e8c15342f27bb2ac1d56bbac0f146b7276338f` |
| `tools/compat/logic-pro/run_baseline.py` Git blob | `f6ae73e2a79138d67643247f21dd067e19bf3e47` |
| `tests/compat/logic-pro/baseline/test_baseline_gate.py` Git blob | `b98cae8e18e91f1442f18d5a2b8e1735bcfc9b88` |
| Parser SHA-256 | `a67ed9e38f731e26e446233fbc65e786ce895dfcb40de75bb944484fb574ee4b` |

The parser and test files were snapshotted before execution. The probe verifies the parser snapshot's Git blob hash before extracting and executing its function AST. I rechecked both working-tree blob hashes after testing; both remained unchanged. This verdict applies to a replacement candidate containing these reviewed blobs. It does not convert the failed base candidate into a pass or certify unrelated changes or full hosted CI.

## Hosted failure confirmed

I independently verified `/workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w4-runtime-artifacts/p003-fixtures-A.zip`, whose SHA-256 is `36aa3a8a3a3e55573cd5621e29a71baa61341dc5129e5c59501714b96e9683a3`. Its `baseline.log` reports 184 tests with six failing subcases, covering class/module setup, teardown, and cleanup in `test_lifecycle_stdout_without_newline_cannot_hide_a_skip`.

The Python 3.10 renderer can append a bare `skipped 'reason'` status after diagnostic stdout without a newline; unlike newer output, that status has no lifecycle label. The prior lifecycle-label search therefore could not detect these outcomes after a forged final `OK`.

## Patch review

The patch introduces a quoted skip-status suffix matcher and checks it before the lifecycle/error fallback paths. It recognizes both single-quoted and double-quoted reason representations, including empty reasons. Existing requirements for one summary, plain final `OK`, matching unique announcement count, per-test completion, ordinary non-success outcomes, and error headers remain intact.

The added repository regression explicitly covers Python 3.10-shaped transcripts with single-quoted, double-quoted, and empty reasons. My additional probes use genuine unittest execution under the installed Python 3.10 interpreter, rather than relying only on hand-assembled transcripts or renderer emulation.

## Independent test results

| Execution | Cases | Negative cases correctly rejected | Successful cases accepted | Known successful cases conservatively rejected | Incorrect acceptances |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Actual CPython 3.10.22 | 78 | 64 | 8 | 6 | 0 |
| Actual CPython 3.12.14 | 78 | 64 | 8 | 6 | 0 |
| Official CPython 3.10.12 renderer with CPython 3.10.22 suite/result facilities | 24 | 24 | N/A | N/A | 0 |

The 78-case runs retain the prior 48-case investigation and add 30 genuine lifecycle/cleanup skip cases: class and module setup, teardown, and cleanup for five reasons (empty, apostrophe, double quote, both quote types, and an embedded newline).

Covered negative behaviors include ordinary failure, failing subtest, method skip, expected failure, unexpected success, class/module lifecycle and cleanup errors/skips, and loader import failure. Only terminal summary text is changed to plain `OK` in the forged-transcript probes; original outcome records and counts remain intact.

For supplemental version-specific verification, I independently executed the reusable renderer probe supplied by `/root/w4_runtime_review`, after inspecting its code. It uses the official CPython v3.10.12 `unittest/runner.py`, fetched from:

<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.10.12/Lib/unittest/runner.py>

Its source SHA-256 is `7ab57b963cd64f210d5a074b15e8dae9b4d1699da980dd523362d3f88e966847`. The 24 supplemental cases all rejected against the same parser SHA-256. This is execution of that renderer under CPython 3.10.22, not a claim that the actual CPython 3.10.12 interpreter was installed.

### Original records preserved on both runtimes

| Original log | Accepted records |
|---|---:|
| baseline.log | 175 |
| build.log | 225 |
| evidence.log | 36 |
| harness.log | 99 |
| submodules.log | 116 |
| **Total** | **651** |

Original logs: `/workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/p004-artifacts/p004-source-00b172d8b1363c2f21deb3cbd0fb29a908ea86fc`.

## Remaining limits

Six genuinely successful class/module setup, teardown, and cleanup cases still reject when stdout without a newline prefixes the next test announcement. This is the previously documented behavior, reproduced on both runtimes; it remains unchanged and does not affect the original logs. The table distinguishes those conservative rejections from passing ideal expectations.

Legacy suffix recognition is necessarily conservative for merged text: unrelated diagnostic output that itself ends in a quoted skip-status shape can also be treated as a skip. This is a scope observation from the matcher, not a claim that such text exists in the original accepted logs.

This review does not independently rerun or certify the root's full 185-test baseline or 108-test harness suites. The root is handling those gates. Transcript consistency validation cannot authenticate an entirely fabricated, internally consistent log; provenance checks remain separate.

## Reproduction

```sh
/workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/python310/cpython-3.10.22-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/python3.10 -B /workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w3_transcript_python310_probe.py /workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w3_transcript_python310_probe-3.10.json
python3 -B /workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w3_transcript_python310_probe.py /workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w3_transcript_python310_probe-3.12.json
/workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/python310/cpython-3.10.22-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/python3.10 -B /workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w4-runtime-artifacts/reviewer/legacy_renderer_probe.py --output /workspace/scratch/28ff48ed8b8b/w3_transcript_python310_renderer-v3.10.12.json
```

The first two commands use the frozen parser snapshot. The supplemental peer script reads the current parser; its result records the parser SHA-256, which was verified against the snapshot. All generated results and execution logs are stored alongside this report. The independent probe's exit status indicates successful completion; its `expected_accept` and `accepted` fields retain the six documented conservative mismatches.

## Provenance and changes

I reviewed repository code, genuine local unittest behavior, the failed hosted artifact, and the official PSF-licensed CPython renderer used solely for this scratch verification. No third-party implementation was added to the repository. No restricted material was used. No repository files or Git state were changed by this review.
